cravada-fc.title: Cravada FC
cravada-fc.short_desc: A free football score-prediction game, live at cravadafc.com: players call the exact score before kickoff, earn points round by round and compete in rankings against the whole country, their club's fans and their friends.
cravada-fc.tagline: Football predictions among friends, no betting and no credit card
cravada-fc.overview: Cravada FC is a real product in production that I built with my friend Guilherme Laureano: he owns product, design and front end, and I own the backend and the database. Before every Brasileirão, Premier League or Champions League match, players call the score. Nail the exact score and you get 5 points; get only the outcome right and you get 3. Points feed the Liga Cravada, which includes every player, a league for each club's fans and private leagues joined by code, with reactions to picks, rival duels and titles like King and Jinx of the round.
cravada-fc.stack_text: Front end in Next.js 15 with React 19 and TypeScript, hand-written CSS following atomic design and BEM, installable as a PWA, with share images drawn on canvas and WhatsApp previews through next/og. Supabase is the source of truth: Postgres with RLS, Auth with email, magic link and Google, pg_cron, pg_net, Vault and a web push Edge Function. An Express and TypeScript backend, running as a Vercel function, serves public match data: standings, line-ups, goals and the live minute.
cravada-fc.architecture_text: Every rule that matters lives in the database. The browser talks straight to Postgres through security definer RPC functions with an empty search_path and auth.uid() checks, while the tables stay closed to the API. Locking picks at kickoff is a trigger, so it cannot be bypassed from the client, and who can see whose picks is also decided in the database. pg_cron jobs sync matches, score predictions, rebuild rankings only when something changed and send push reminders. Secrets such as VAPID keys and the Telegram token live in Vault, never in the repository or the front end.
cravada-fc.challenges_text: Scoring every prediction as soon as a match ends without keeping a server running all the time. The answer was a pipeline inside Postgres itself: one cron asks for the open rounds, another applies the results and calls the scoring function, and rankings sit in a materialized cache that is only rebuilt when something changed, keeping queries fast even in large leagues. The other challenge was making the social side safe: private leagues with invite codes, nickname moderation with blocked terms, bans by the league owner and visibility rules that only reveal picks once the ball is rolling.
cravada-fc.metric_highlight: 3 competitions (Brasileirão, Premier League and Champions League), points settled within a minute of the final whistle and 5 scheduled Postgres jobs handling matches, rankings and notifications with no dedicated server.

cwu-app.title: CWU App
cwu-app.short_desc: A Windows app that combines post-install setup and gaming optimization: it reads the real hardware, batch-installs the essentials through winget and applies explained tweaks, all logged and reversible.
cwu-app.tagline: Windows post-install setup and gaming optimization, no placebo
cwu-app.overview: After formatting a PC you lose hours installing drivers and programs and hunting for "optimizations" that mostly do nothing. CWU App (Chico Wagner Utility, named after my cat) gathers what actually works: hardware diagnostics with a 0-10 score, drive health via SMART, driver checks through Windows Update and NVIDIA, a software catalog with batch install, error and blue-screen analysis, gaming tweaks and an FPS overlay. Project rule: no made-up data, no magic FPS promises, and everything reversible.
cwu-app.stack_text: Electron for the window, a plain HTML, CSS (BEMIT) and JavaScript frontend, and a Node.js server built only on native modules, with zero production dependencies. Windows access goes through PowerShell, WMI/CIM, the registry and winget. Optional accounts and the AI assistant (Gemini) run on Supabase, with the AI key kept in an Edge Function and never shipped in the app.
cwu-app.architecture_text: The local server follows routes → controllers → services and listens on 127.0.0.1 only. Since the app runs as administrator, the API was treated as an attack surface: a random per-run token in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie compared in constant time, Host and Origin allow-lists against CSRF and DNS rebinding, a Content-Security-Policy with no inline scripts, and PowerShell actions limited to a closed list with validated parameters.
cwu-app.challenges_text: Reading real-time metrics without slowing down the very PC being optimized. Spawning one PowerShell process per reading was expensive, so the monitor uses a single long-running process that streams every metric, and each tab only fetches data when it is opened. The other challenge was trust: every change asks for confirmation, is logged in the history and can be reverted, and the app offers to create a restore point before the first change.
cwu-app.metric_highlight: 86 automated tests on GitHub Actions on every push, zero production dependencies on the server and auto-updates verified by SHA-512.

time-tracker.title: Time Trackerígena
time-tracker.short_desc: Full-stack time and operational tracking platform featuring Flask/Python backend, relational persistence, and a rapid, responsive interface built with React and TypeScript.
time-tracker.overview: Time Trackerígena is an operational governance platform designed for activity logging, team capacity tracking, and real-time analytical productivity reporting. Built to eliminate concurrency issues in timesheet submissions while providing instant management metrics.
time-tracker.stack_text: Structured Python backend using Flask and SQLAlchemy for relational persistence over PostgreSQL/SQLite, ensuring transactional ACID guarantees and robust migration lifecycles with Alembic. Decoupled React + TypeScript frontend utilizing typed API client services and modular interactive calendar components.
time-tracker.architecture_text: Clean layered architecture enforcing strict separation between HTTP route handlers, domain service logic, and persistence repositories. Composite indices on temporal fields and foreign keys optimize aggregate hour computations and monthly summaries without database table locks.
time-tracker.challenges_text: Managing cross-timezone calculation and batch recalculation of accumulated hours on the client side without triggering unnecessary re-renders across the monthly calendar matrix. Resolved via state normalization, strategic memoization, and weekly paginated payload structures.
time-tracker.metric_highlight: 140+ logged hours/month per user with zero concurrency errors and average API response time < 45ms.

ai-assistant-integrator.title: AI Integrator & Organic Chatbot
ai-assistant-integrator.short_desc: Multi-provider AI orchestration platform (Gemini, OpenAI, Groq, and resident simulator Ozlo) with real-time SSE streaming, live latency & token metrics, and accessible UI.
ai-assistant-integrator.tagline: Asynchronous SSE streaming, multi-model RAG and metrics
ai-assistant-integrator.overview: Advanced multi-provider orchestration platform spanning Google Gemini, OpenAI GPT, and Groq Llama, paired with an integrated resident intelligence simulator (Ozlo). Provides asynchronous token-by-token streaming, latency telemetry, and a diagnostics dashboard for production AI apps.
ai-assistant-integrator.stack_text: Asynchronous Python 3.12 backend powered by FastAPI, leveraging asyncio and Server-Sent Events (SSE) for low-latency continuous payload delivery. React and TypeScript client featuring custom chunk parsing, adaptive buffer management, and live telemetry tracking (Time-to-First-Token and Tokens/second).
ai-assistant-integrator.architecture_text: Adapter and Factory patterns isolating vendor-specific API contracts. An integrated circuit-breaker gracefully triggers automated fallback when upstream LLM providers encounter timeouts or rate limits (HTTP 429), maintaining zero disruption for end users.
ai-assistant-integrator.challenges_text: Sustaining 60 FPS rendering of Markdown and syntax-highlighted code blocks while incoming tokens arrive in rapid bursts over the SSE stream. Solved via adaptive chunk buffering throttle and targeted React virtualization.
ai-assistant-integrator.metric_highlight: SSE streaming with average TTFT (Time-to-First-Token) of 184ms and fully autonomous circuit-breaker fallback.
